item.title: Offset Points To November 13 For GMFU After October 23 Plan
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Offset pointed to November 13 for GMFU in an Instagram post after his label had announced the album for October 23.
item.content:encoded:
Offset appeared to move GMFU to November 13, pushing the album three weeks past the October 23 release his label announced.

The rapper posted “GMFU 11:13 @gotmefukkkedup” on Instagram, and he did not explain the change in the caption.

The first image in the carousel showed the letters GMFU being embroidered on a camouflage hat.

His label’s October 9 announcement had introduced the album alongside “Every Night,” his latest song with Don Toliver, and listed Motown Records as its home.

That announcement gave October 23 as the release date, rather than the November date now suggested by his post.

Jaasu produced “Every Night,” which samples Jodeci’s 1995 song “Freek’n You.” Mikey Rare and SheShe Pendleton directed its casino-set video.

The single followed September’s “Something I Need,” with production from Southside, Smatt Sertified and Jester Beats.

Toliver has been part of Offset’s solo music for years.

They took “Worth It,” from Offset’s second solo album Set It Off, to “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” for its Thanksgiving episode in November 2023.

Offset also appeared on “Had Enough,” a song included on Toliver’s Heaven or Hell.

The next album follows KIARI and its expanded edition, both released in 2025.

Named for Offset’s first name, KIARI got a Times Square unveiling on August 4 that year. Its early singles included “Bodies” with JID and “Professional.”

The deluxe version added a BNYX remix of “Bodies.” Other collaborations on KIARI included “Different Species” with Gunna, “Back in That Mode” with YFN Lucci and “Run It Up” with Key Glock, each of which also received a video.

The album plans came as Offset and Quavo were working together again.

Their song “Away” appeared on Quavo’s QRÖMELIFE, which arrived October 2.

Separate projects for Migos and Takeoff were still being prepared, Quavo said. He also traced his history with Offset back to seventh grade.

To him, the “Away” session helped them reconnect and brought back the chemistry they had in their school days.

item.title: Chrisean Rock Teases November 20 Fight While Showing Off $800K Earnings
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Chrisean Rock teased another fight on Kick, but the title and a clip's November 20 caption did not name an opponent.
item.content:encoded:
Chrisean Rock teased a return to the ring on Kick, with a November 20 date attached to her upcoming bout.

Three recent recordings on her verified channel used “chat I’ll be fighting the 20th” as their title. That wording gave a day, but no month or opponent.

A November 20 event lists Rock’s name, though the public billing lists her as a host.

Official Celebrity Boxing promoted Influencer Fight Night at Harrah’s Philadelphia Casino in Chester, Pennsylvania, with Rock and Justina Valentine hosting. The event is scheduled to begin at 7 P.M.

That listing didn’t name a Rock opponent or say she would compete, but her desire to get in the ring is understandable given how much money she made in her last fight.

She showed her live audience the massive amount of money she raked in – over $849,000, while showing off her global audience metrics.

.

Chrisean Rock has fought in both a crossover bout and a pro match this year. Her boxing plans first took her to XRumble. In January, she signed with promoter Damon Feldman.

Her manager, Kimberly Ross, joined her at the signing. On April 25, she faced Zenith Zion at Harrah’s Philadelphia. Zion brought a background in pro wrestling and slap fighting to the bout. She won that crossover contest by split decision.

The April win did not count as a pro victory.

Before her next fight, she announced she had earned her pro license and laid out her goal: facing pro boxers, not celebrities.

To prepare, she trained with Calvin Ford, Gervonta Davis’s longtime trainer. Fighting as Chrisean “Holy Hands” Malone, she made her pro debut on September 19 against Ku’Shiyah Williams.

Neither woman had a pro record before they met in the ring.

The bout took place at the Hyatt Regency Baltimore Inner Harbor. It was part of Skyy Myles Promotions’ “The Supper” card on BLK Prime pay-per-view.

Chrisean Rock stopped Williams in the second round by TKO. She ended the night 1-0 as a pro.

item.title: Kendrick Lamar Sneaks In Jay-Z’s JAŸ-Z30 Celebration
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Kendrick Lamar joined a celebrity audience as Jay-Z celebrated 30 years of Hip-Hop greatness at SoFi Stadium, with a warning about AI.
item.content:encoded:
He did not really sneak in, but I am almost sure Kendrick Lamar had a side entrance apart from everybody else. And there were a lot of “everybody else’s” there.

K-Dot pulled up to support Jay-Z at SoFi Stadium, where the Brooklyn billionaire transformed Los Angeles into a celebration of Hip-Hop history, family and an extraordinary musical legacy.

The Compton superstar was reportedly among the celebrities watching the first night of the JAŸ-Z30 celebration on Friday, October 23. And while K-Dot did not join Hov onstage, his presence was another reminder of the respect Jay-Z commands across generations of Hip-Hop.

The sold-out concert was the first of two Los Angeles performances commemorating 30 years of Reasonable Doubt and 25 years of The Blueprint. After stops in New York, London and Paris, Hov arrived in California with plenty of classics and a few surprises.

Opening with “Hovi Baby,” Jay-Z delivered a sprawling performance that included “Izzo,” “Run This Town,” “Hard Knock Life,” “Dirt Off Your Shoulder” and “99 Problems.” A full live band, complete with horns and strings, gave the familiar records additional muscle.

One of the evening’s most touching moments came when Blue Ivy Carter accompanied her father on piano for “Dead Presidents” and “The Story of O.J.” Beyoncé watched from the audience alongside her Destiny’s Child sisters Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams.

Houston legend Scarface joined Jay-Z for “This Can’t Be Life” and the Geto Boys classic “Mind Playing Tricks On Me.” John Legend and DJ Khaled also appeared, helping close the evening with “God Did.”

Hov made sure Los Angeles received some hometown love, incorporating Nipsey Hussle’s “Hussle & Motivate” and “Last Time I Checc’d” into his performance. The tribute connected two influential figures whose music has resonated far beyond their respective neighborhoods.

Rihanna, Tia Mowry, G-Eazy and Omari Hardwick were also among the famous faces reportedly in attendance.

The concert was a reminder that Jay-Z’s catalog has become something bigger than a collection of hits. Three decades into his recording career, the Brooklyn MC can still command a stadium while bringing together artists, entertainers and fans from different eras.

item.title: Jay-Z Brings Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg & Too $hort To SoFi Finale
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jay-Z celebrates three decades of music at SoFi as Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too $hort join his final anniversary concert.
item.content:encoded:
Jay-Z brought Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too $hort to his SoFi Stadium finale Saturday for a night packed with West Coast classics.

The October 24 show capped his anniversary concert series in Inglewood with a sold-out crowd and songs from across his career.

Snoop performed “Murder Was the Case” before Dre joined him for a guest set that drew on their shared catalog. The pair performed “California Love” and “Still D.R.E.,” plus “The Next Episode” and “Nuthin’ but a ‘G’ Thang.”

Too $hort had helped get the night started with “Blow the Whistle” after Jay opened the show with “The Watcher 2.”

Jay also honored Nipsey Hussle by displaying his image on the screen and weaving his music into the set. The tribute included “Hussle & Motivate,” while “On to the Next One” featured the instrumental from “Last Time That I Checc’d.”

USA Today reporter Caché McClay placed Jay’s arrival at about 9:25 p.m. before he greeted the stadium crowd.

“Thank you for being here tonight. Tonight is special.”

His own selections ranged from “Dead Presidents” and “D’Evils” to “Song Cry,” with “Never Change” also in the set.

There was room for “99 Problems” and “Money, Cash, Hoes,” along with “Girls, Girls, Girls” and “Excuse Me Miss.” He finished with “Empire State of Mind,” “Big Pimpin’,” “Public Service Announcement,” and “Encore” as the last four songs.

Friday offered another set of guests as Blue Ivy Carter played piano for her father during “The Story of O.J.” and “Dead Presidents.”

Scarface joined him for “This Can’t Be Life” and “Mind Playing Tricks on Me” during the first of the two SoFi shows. John Legend and DJ Khaled closed Friday with “God Did” after Jay opened the night with “Hovi Baby.”

Beyoncé watched Friday from a suite with Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams, giving the crowd an offstage Destiny’s Child reunion.

The run marked 30 years since Reasonable Doubt and 25 since The Blueprint, with earlier shows in New York, London and Paris.

For Saturday’s finale, June Ambrose designed the custom looks Jay wore as he moved through the night’s songs and guest appearances.

item.title: Nicki Minaj Takes Her Trump Support To Michigan Campaign Trail
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Nicki Minaj is expected alongside Donald Trump in Port Huron as Michigan's Senate contest draws major campaign attention.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj is taking her support for Donald Trump onto Michigan’s campaign trail with a reported rally appearance on Sunday.

The Washington Examiner reported that she will appear with the president in Port Huron to help Republicans seeking office. Former Rep. Mike Rogers is among those candidates as he seeks Michigan’s open Senate seat in the November 3 election.

Trump’s rally is scheduled at McMorran Place Arena, with doors opening at 11:30 a.m. Eastern, according to FOX 2 Detroit.

The visit comes nine days before Election Day and follows months of Minaj publicly defending her ties to the president.

At a January 28 event for Trump Accounts, Minaj defended her support for the president and addressed criticism of their alliance.

“And that’s not going to change. And the hate, or what people have to say, it does not affect me at all,” she said, according to TheWrap.

Her support continued during a September 18 appearance on The Ingraham Angle alongside Small Business Administration head Kelly Loeffler.

Asked about their connection during that interview, Minaj spoke about how she felt when she watched Trump interact with people.

“It’s easy to connect with him. It’s easy to feel like he heard you. He understands you. I just love him.”

Minaj also said she wanted her concerts to give people good memories and a chance to enjoy music without political lectures.

That September interview came as she took a judging role in the Million Dollar Pitch Competition for small business owners. She joined Grant Cardone and Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia on the panel for a competition offering a $1 million prize pool.

Sunday’s campaign stop puts her support behind a Republican Senate hopeful who faces Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in a closely watched race.

Reuters reported that the contest could help decide Senate control as Republicans defend their current majority of 53 seats to 47. Former President Barack Obama appeared in Detroit on Saturday to urge support for Democrats as both parties chased votes across Michigan.

Trump is scheduled to begin his remarks at 3 p.m. Eastern on Sunday, according to the local station’s rally information.

item.title: FAMU Homecoming Weekend Turns Violent With 12 People Hurt
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Florida A&M University faces a painful homecoming aftermath as police search for those responsible for wounding children and adults.
item.content:encoded:
Florida A&M University’s homecoming weekend turned violent Saturday when 11 people were shot near the Tallahassee campus and another person was hurt fleeing.

Six children were among the 12 injured after the football game, with the youngest victim just 11 years old, police said.

Officers responded shortly before 8 p.m. October 24 near Perry and Manatee streets, close to the university’s Bragg Memorial Stadium.

Police said their early investigation pointed to a fight before the shooting, but detectives were still working to identify those responsible.

At their overnight news conference, authorities had announced no arrests and had not identified a person of interest, WCTV reported.

The injuries ranged in severity, with WCTV reporting one person in critical condition, three seriously hurt and eight others stable.

That account followed an earlier police statement that listed at least three victims with serious injuries and nine in stable condition.

“It is especially heartbreaking to know that children are among those injured,” Tallahassee Police Chief Lawrence Revell said.

Revell said he believed one victim was a FAMU student, according to WCTV, though that person’s enrollment had not been confirmed.

About two dozen officers were nearby before the shooting, and Revell said the department’s entire force was working the busy weekend.

Officers carried wounded people away from danger and helped get them to the hospital before the scene was secure, Revell said.

FAMU said its campus remained safe after the shooting and urged people to avoid the area while police investigated.

The university also encouraged anyone who knew something about the incident to share that information with Tallahassee police.

Homecoming activities had included a student aid initiative involving Gunna, whose Wunna Run Club joined Walmart in a $10,000 scholarship pledge.

The partnership tied to the October 22 homecoming 5K designated five $2,000 awards for students pursuing majors with a health component.

The police department’s Violent Crimes Unit took over the shooting investigation, with detectives gathering evidence and speaking with witnesses about what happened.

Anyone with information can reach investigators at 850-891-4200 or provide an anonymous tip through Crime Solvers at 850-574-TIPS.

item.title: Man Arrested After Alleged Knife Threat At Michael B. Jordan’s “Miami Vice ’85” Set
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Michael B. Jordan's "Miami Vice '85" shoot was reportedly disrupted after a man allegedly threatened a crew member with a butcher knife.
item.content:encoded:
Michael B. Jordan‘s “Miami Vice ’85” production was reportedly disrupted Friday night after a man allegedly threatened a crew member with a butcher knife in Brooklyn.

According to TMZ, which cited the NYPD, police arrested Alex Perez, 23, at 11:17 P.M. on October 23.

He was charged with second-degree menacing with a weapon and fourth-degree criminal possession of a weapon.

The outlet reported that Perez ran across the set around 11 P.M. and that police were called after he allegedly displayed the knife and threatened a production staffer.

TMZ also published footage it said showed a staff member escorting Perez away before he reached into his sweatshirt pocket and pulled out the knife.

The report said Perez used a racial slur toward the worker while handcuffed.

It was unclear Jordan was present during the confrontation or identify him as the person threatened.

The arrest came as the new film’s New York shoot was drawing attention.

Earlier Friday, ABC7 reporter Phil Taitt published his account of spotting Jordan filming near City Hall, a separate New York location from the Brooklyn set named in the arrest report.

Jordan plays detective Ricardo Tubbs opposite Austin Butler’s Sonny Crockett. The pair take over roles made famous by Philip Michael Thomas and Don Johnson on the original television series, which ran from 1984 to 1989.

Joseph Kosinski, the director behind “Top Gun: Maverick” and “F1,” is making the new version for IMAX.

Rather than updating the detectives for the present day, this film takes them back to Miami in the mid-1980s. Its story draws on the show’s pilot and first season, according to “Good Morning America”.

Dan Gilroy wrote the script. His credits include “Nightcrawler,” “Kong: Skull Island” and episodes of the Star Wars series “Andor.”

This is the second big-screen version of the series.

Jamie Foxx played Tubbs alongside Colin Farrell’s Crockett in Michael Mann’s 2006 “Miami Vice.”

Universal has released the first photos of Jordan and Butler in character.

“Miami Vice ’85” is scheduled to reach theaters on May 19, 2028.

item.title: Latto’s BBL Has The Internet A-Talking, But Why Was The Video Deleted?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Latto's BBL has the internet divided after a provocative video reportedly disappeared, leaving fans wondering what really happened.
item.content:encoded:
Latto has never hidden her BBL from the people. We know she got it at 21, and now, at 27, I guess she has mastered it!

In a video circulating online, Big Mama goes off with the muscles back there. And I must say, it’s quite impressive! But apparently, not everybody agrees. The clip has sparked some controversy, and there are questions about why the original video seemingly disappeared.

So, here we are.

In the footage, Latto is wearing a thong-style outfit with what appears to be sheer pantyhose material. She’s dancing, moving around and seemingly quite proud of what she’s working with. And why shouldn’t she be?

The internet does what it does.

One side is saying she’s the GOAT, solely based on her backside. In fact, some of these folks are saying she’s been the best in the business for about five years! I never knew. These have GOT to be her biggest fans.

Now, there’s another side.

The other side of the coin consists of a group we’ll uniformly call the “haters.” They’re saying her booty looks a bit too jiggly and offering all sorts of other critiques. Now, I’m not sure if this is BBL shaming or something else, but a number of women appear to be among those criticizing her.

This is not science, but there seems to be a visceral response to her tail feather!

What’s particularly interesting is that Latto has already addressed this very issue. Back in 2024, she admitted that she underwent a Brazilian butt lift at 21 after negative comments about her body made her insecure. She even suggested that the same internet that pressured her into getting the procedure eventually criticized her for having it.

You really cannot win with these people!

Anyway, Big Mama is out here working! She’s got an infant daughter, a rapper man in 21 Savage and an empire to build. And somehow, she’s still got time for the haters!

Now, I don’t know who originally posted the video or exactly why it was reportedly taken down. If Latto posted it herself, perhaps she caught wind of the drama and decided enough was enough. That’s certainly possible, but we don’t know.

Or could there be another reason?

What if, for example, 21 Savage didn’t particularly appreciate the video being out there?

Hmmmmm…

Before anybody starts running with that, let me be clear. I have absolutely no evidence that 21 Savage had anything to do with the video’s disappearance. That’s simply a question, not an allegation.

And considering these two have been showing off their family life publicly, I wouldn’t automatically assume there’s trouble in paradise.

But you know how the internet works. One minute, everybody’s admiring the scenery. The next minute, we’re investigating a missing video like it’s a federal case!

For now, that’s all we’ve got.

There’s also a bigger story here. The BBL has become one of the most debated beauty trends in modern Hip-Hop, and Latto has been unusually transparent about her experience. In a 2023 interview with Cosmopolitan, she revealed that she underwent a BBL and 360 liposuction in 2020. She also discussed hiring a personal trainer to maintain her physique rather than undergoing another procedure. By 2024, she was openly discussing how online criticism influenced her original decision. That history makes the latest reaction particularly ironic. The same public that criticized her natural body continues to debate the results of her surgery years later. I think this vid all came from her ongoing tour with Doja Cat.

What do you think? Is Latto being unfairly criticized, or is this simply what happens when celebrities put it all out there? And why do you think the video disappeared? Sound off in the comments!

item.title: Macklemore Takes Palestine Message Back To The Stage At Red Rocks
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Macklemore renewed his Palestine advocacy and criticized ICE at Red Rocks after his removal from Ed Sheeran's tour.
item.content:encoded:
Macklemore renewed his support for Palestinians and criticized ICE at Red Rocks Amphitheatre, returning to the stage after being removed from his remaining opening dates for Ed Sheeran.

The Seattle rapper performed at the Colorado venue on October 22.

He urged the crowd to see the suffering of others as a human concern rather than a political divide.

“Being a human being in this moment is not complicated,” Macklemore said. “It is not political. It is human to have a heart to watch others suffer and to say not any more.”

The crowd erupted in cheers as he continued his message of solidarity.

“I say free Palestine,” he declared, extending his call for liberation beyond a single cause.

“I say free Sudan. I say free Congo, Lebanon, to Haiti. To all the people that are affected by ICE in America, that are afraid to leave their houses.”

“The message will always be love,” he said.

The concert followed a dispute over what he said while opening for Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey in September.

During those appearances, he called for Palestinian freedom and performed “Hind’s Hall,” his protest song released in 2024.

New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft objected to having him perform at Gillette Stadium.

Kraft said his concerns involved both the New Jersey performances and what he described as a history of rhetoric and imagery offensive to Jewish people.

The rapper rejected the idea that his message targeted Jewish people. He distinguished criticism of Israel from criticism of Jewish people and called for equal treatment.

He had also criticized ICE during that earlier speech.

After his removal, Sheeran’s other announced supporting acts withdrew in solidarity.

Sheeran said the decision came from the tour’s organizers and that he had tried to resolve the dispute. He later apologized for his handling of it during a Philadelphia concert.

The fallout also led to a financial pledge. Macklemore committed his $1 million in net earnings from the Sheeran dates to six organizations supporting Palestinians and challenged Kraft to match him.

Kraft said he had already committed $2 million for humanitarian aid in the region.

In his public announcement for the benefit concerts, Macklemore said the dispute went beyond his own career or access to a stage.

A separate series of “Free Palestine” benefit concerts is scheduled to begin at Dublin’s 3Arena on October 26, followed by Paris’ Accor Arena on October 29 and London’s OVO Arena Wembley on October 30. Proceeds are intended for organizations supporting Palestinians.

item.title: Missy Elliott Tells Dancers They’re Artists As Cancer Gala Raises Over $760K
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Missy Elliott honored dancers in her Icon Award speech as the Gala of the Stars raised more than $760,000 for cancer support.
item.content:encoded:
Missy Elliott put dancers at the center of her Icon Award speech earlier this week, calling them artists rather than stage props.

The rapper accepted the honor at the October 22 Gala of the Stars at The Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills, California. The benefit raised more than $760,000 for Dancers Against Cancer, organizers said in a release.

Janet Jackson, who received the same honor in 2025, presented Missy with the award. Missy’s acceptance speech focused on the work that dancers bring to an artist’s show.

“Dancers are not just props on a stage behind artists. What y’all give is energy, emotion, expression, excitement, entertainment to an artist’s show. You bring life to an artist’s lyrics on that stage. Y’all are artists too! Because it takes incredible skill, dedication, discipline, practice and passion to do what you do,” Missy said.

Jackson’s presentation touched on that same bond between the music and the people who bring it to the stage.

“Missy Elliott helped make dancers impossible to ignore,” Jackson said. She credited Missy with elevating choreography and encouraging dancers to embrace their individuality.

At Thursday’s gala, Anthony Kanec performed a dance tribute to Missy. Maks Chmerkovskiy hosted the benefit, which also honored Toni Basil with its Lifetime Achievement Award and Vincent Paterson with its Vanguard Award.

Paula Abdul presented the Paula Abdul Legacy Award in a posthumous tribute to Chita Rivera. Hilaria Baldwin received the Philanthropist of the Year Award.

Organizers said the money raised would help dancers, choreographers, educators, and their families affected by cancer.
